mathgap.title: Sequential processing of transfers
mathgap.principle: When a transfer statement appears, immediately adjust both the giver's and receiver's counts: subtract the transferred amount from the giver and add it to the receiver, and use these updated counts for any later statements.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement of the form 'X gives N items to Y' is encountered.
mathgap.example: Treating a transfer as a static equation X = Y + N instead of updating X and Y, causing later references to use outdated values.

mathgap.title: Signed difference equality
mathgap.principle: Translate statements that equate a signed difference to another difference as (A - B) = (C - D), preserving the order of names on each side.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement says 'the number of X that Y has more than Z is equal to the difference between the number of A and B' (or similar).
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'difference between A and B' as |A - B| (absolute) and swapping the order, losing the sign information.

mathgap.title: Direct count assignment at point of mention
mathgap.principle: When a statement directly gives a count for a person (e.g., 'X has N items'), set that person's current count to N at that point in the sequence.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement provides an explicit numeric count for a person.
mathgap.example: Ignoring an explicit count and treating it as a relative statement, leading to ambiguous or conflicting values later on.

mathgap.title: Non‑negative integer check
mathgap.principle: All item counts must be non‑negative integers; discard any solution that yields a negative or fractional count.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After solving the equations, verify that each variable satisfies the non‑negative integer constraint.
mathgap.example: Accepting a solution where a person ends up with -3 carrots, which is impossible.

mathgap.title: Conditional transfer handling
mathgap.principle: For conditional transfers, first evaluate the condition using the current counts; only if the condition holds, perform the transfer.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement includes a condition like 'if X has at least N items, X gives N to Y'.
mathgap.example: Always performing the transfer regardless of the condition, causing negative counts or contradictions.

mathgap.title: Redistribution equalization handling
mathgap.principle: When a statement says two persons redistribute items to ensure each has an equal amount, pool their items and split them evenly, discarding any remainder.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement describes equalizing counts between two people.
mathgap.example: Leaving the original owner with all items after redistribution, instead of splitting them equally.

mathgap.title: Multiplicative increase handling
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'the number of X increases by N times', multiply X's current count by N (i.e., X = X * N).
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement uses phrasing like 'increases by N times' or 'is multiplied by N'.
mathgap.example: Treating 'increases by 3 times' as adding 3 instead of multiplying by 3.

mathgap.title: Directionality of more/fewer statements
mathgap.principle: Interpret 'X has N more than Y' as X - Y = N (i.e., X = Y + N) and 'X has N fewer than Y' as X - Y = -N (i.e., X = Y - N).
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement uses 'more' or 'fewer' to compare counts.
mathgap.example: Reversing the direction and setting Y = X + N instead of X = Y + N.

mathgap.title: Split-all handling
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'X splits all the items she owns equally among Y and Z', give each of Y and Z floor(count_X / 2) items, and set X's count to the remainder (if any).
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement describes splitting all items of a person equally among two others.
mathgap.example: Leaving the original person with zero items after splitting, even when there is an odd remainder that should stay.

mathgap.title: Targeted constraint extraction for queried variable
mathgap.principle: When the goal is to find a specific person's count, first collect all statements that directly involve that person (including as part of a difference equality) and solve those equations, using other constraints only to determine the other variables appearing in those equations. This reduces the problem size and avoids being misled by extraneous constraints.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever the problem asks for the count of a particular individual and the problem contains many unrelated statements.
mathgap.example: Attempting to solve the entire system of equations, leading to sign errors or misapplied transfers, instead of focusing on the equations that involve the queried person.

mathgap.description: Treating signed difference statements as absolute differences
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes 'difference between A and B' means |A - B|, losing the sign and order.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always preserve the order of names and treat the difference as a signed subtraction (A - B).

mathgap.description: Ignoring the sequential order of transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model applies transfers out of order or treats them as static equations, not updating counts for later statements.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Process transfer statements in the order they appear, updating the giver and receiver before any subsequent statements.

mathgap.description: Assuming explicit counts are final after all transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats a direct count assignment as the final value, ignoring later transfers that modify the count.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat explicit counts as the current count at that point; apply any later transfers to update the count.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting 'increase by N times' as addition rather than multiplication
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model reads 'increase by N times' as adding N instead of multiplying by N.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Interpret 'increase by N times' as multiplication: new count = old count * N.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting split-all statements as leaving the original person with zero even when they are a recipient
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model incorrectly discards the remainder or assumes the original person loses all items.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When splitting, give each recipient floor(count/2) and keep the remainder with the original person.
